The Scheduling Zoo, non-preemptive problems on parallel machines

      Natural Language Statement

      Theorem

      The 256 non-preemptive problems on parallel machines of The Scheduling Zoo, each as a specification, and the 251 relations of the zoo among them that are derived here.

      A relation of the zoo states that one problem generalizes another. The 242 relations of the first list hold field by field, so that the more special problem is a special case of the more general one. The 9 relations of the second list need a threshold step, so that the decision version of the more special problem reduces to that of the more general one. The 0 relations of the third list replace completion time by flow time and likewise give a reduction of decision versions. Each pair lists the more general problem first.

      Theorem. Every pair of the first list is a special case, and every pair of the other lists is a reduction of decision versions.
